messages.body_plain:
Your question is not clear.

You ask: what next? the answer is usually that you submit a new revision of the package, so no matter how small the fixes you need to increment the package version number (typically a patchlevel update) to get a response from CRAN.

You ask what to do with an issue? It is extremely difficult for some random person on this list (much less the rare person who might have an answer to your problem) to answer that... you are setting yourself up to be ignored by not providing a CRAN link to the most recent build output that had your implemented fixes. If you don't have this then see the previous paragraph.

This is a generic response by a random non-expert in MKL problems in the hope that with a proper query you can catch the attention of an actual expert. Best of luck...

messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] How to propose TOST 1.0 for R’s license database
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-devel] How to propose TOST 1.0 for R’s license database
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I’m preparing libopenusd for distribution as an R package. It bundles
Pixar’s OpenUSD
(https://github.com/PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD/blob/release/LICENSE.txt)
library, which uses the Tomorrow Open Source Technology License 1.0
(TOST). TOST isn’t listed in R’s license database. SPDX lists the
earlier version under the identifier Pixar
(https://spdx.org/licenses/Pixar.html), and OpenUSD confirmed
(https://forum.aousd.org/t/upcoming-openusd-license-update/1561) that
the rename to TOST didn’t change the terms.

TOST differs from Apache 2.0 only in Section 6 (Trademarks). The
revised clause does not grant permission to use the licensor’s or its
affiliates’ marks except as needed to preserve the required source
notices and reproduce the NOTICE file. The terms for using and
distributing the code are otherwise the same as Apache 2.0, so the
narrower trademark grant seems (to me) like a reasonable and
completely inconsequential limitation for distribution in the R
ecosystem.

What’s the process for proposing that TOST be added to R’s license
database and accepted for CRAN submissions? Who should I send the
proposal to, and what information would be useful for the review?

Best regards,
Tyler Morgan-Wall

messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] Follow-up: Check time > 10min (secr)
messages.body_plain:
Last June I asked here why secr's Windows pre-test overran 10 minutes when the listed steps summed to far less (https://www.mail-archive.com/r-package-devel at r-project.org/msg10774.html). Replies pointed out that Windows does not itemise installation time, which was the missing piece. Thanks to Sebastian Meyer and Joshua Ulrich for that. A report of what fixed it in the end may help others.
For secr 5.6.1, winbuilder R-devel gave installation 312 s and check time 905 s (before the changes below). Two changes made the difference.
1. Combining the C++ files. Each of 21 files took about 3 s to compile regardless of size, because each re-parsed the same headers (Rcpp, RcppParallel, 7 Boost distributions: about 2.6 s of the 3 s). Merging them into one .cpp file cut local install from 107 s to 41 s, and winbuilder installation from 312 s to 84-90 s, check time to 590-649 s. A single file compiled in about 9 s against 65 s for the separate files. I merged into one file rather than a wrapper that #includes the others or a subfolder, because Rcpp::compileAttributes() scans only top-level src/*.cpp and would otherwise lose the exports. -pedantic made no difference to install time.
2. Not importing terra and raster. Every check step that loads the package pays the load time, and on the Windows pre-test machine each load took about 11 s. Loading secr took 2.9 s locally, of which about 2 s was terra and raster. Moving both to Suggests and registering my S4 methods when they are loaded (via setHook(packageEvent(...)), with the methods stored in a private environment, because the namespace is locked) cut that to 0.9 s. Note that raster imports terra, so one without the other saves nothing. On Winbuilder now: installation 58 s and check time 384 s.
The cost is a small API change (users must load raster or terra before calling raster(mask)).
I did this work with the help of Claude (Anthropic's AI assistant), which carried out the timing measurements and drafted the code changes; I reviewed, tested and take responsibility for the results.
Murray Efford

messages.body_plain:
On 21 November 2026 at 12:27, James Pustejovsky wrote:
| We know how to fix the unit tests. We're just struggling to figure out how
| to validate that our corrections will pass. Thanks for any suggestions
| offered!

Replication is always the first step. And for that it used to be more
difficult to get MKL installed -- so I once set up a GitHub repo with a
script at https://github.com/eddelbuettel/mkl4deb to show how to do that
based on the 'upstream' Intel repos for Debian / Ubuntu which (at the time)
were external to the distros.

This repo is now outdated. MKL is now more generally available directly for
Ubuntu (version 2020.4.304-4 and 2020.4.304-7 packaged for 24.04 and 26.04)
and also for Debian (same 2020.4.304-7) thanks to some changes in their
licensing. Regardless the repo of mine still gets hits and stars...

If you prefer a local setup this is another alternative worth exploring.
Now, as always, a possible 'delta' to the CRAN setup is always a possibly.
Sadly CRAN does not make it as easy as it could be to reproduce failings
occurring at their end. Maybe one day we all get to collaborate on genuine
specs and e.g. Dockerfiles to actually pin this down for good.

Dirk

-- 
dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org

messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to unarchive a package. It passes the
usethis::use_github_action() checks on Window release, mac release,
and ubuntu.

When I submit to CRAN it fails on a Debian machine with message
 Debian: <https://win-builder.r-project.org/incoming_pretest/SPAS_2026.12.2_20261127_035904/Debian/00check.log>

which says that
R was compiled by
    Debian clang version 23.1.4 (2)
    Debian flang version 23.1.4 (2)

with error messages
Error(s) in re-building vignettes:
  ...
--- re-building ?AutomaticPooling.Rmd? using rmarkdown
[WARNING] Deprecated: --mathjax. Use --math-method=mathjax[:URL] instead.
Error parsing YAML metadata at "AutomaticPooling.knit.md" (line 1, column 1):
AutomaticPooling.knit.md:11:5: ']' is indented too little to end the
flow sequence
   |
11 |     ]
   |     ^
Error: processing vignette 'AutomaticPooling.Rmd' failed with diagnostics:
pandoc document conversion failed with error 64

Apparently the new Pandoc is more strict about the yaml structure.

I've fixed this, but for the life of me, I can't figure out which
option to use in
   rhub::rhub_check(platforms = xxx)
to see if if I've truely fixed the problem before resubmitting to CRAN.

For example, if i use
    rhub::rhub_check(platforms="ubuntu-clang")
 because it is an [r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-clang] so appears to be
a debian system,but the output says
   * R was compiled by
        gcc (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0
        GNU Fortran (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0
which doesn't appear to be debian???

If I use
  rhub::rhub_check(platforms = "clang23")
to match the clang 23.1.4 in the CRAN error message, it stops because
it cant install the mvtnorm package.

It would be helpful if the CRAN error message somehow identified a
particular system that was used when an error occured to make it
easier to check before resubmission.

Thanks
Carl Schwarz
